question: On long-haul flights, how much did a planned nap in the cockpit seat help pilots later in the flight?
answer: A great deal. Pilots given a 40-minute rest opportunity slept about 26 minutes on average, and later showed 34% better performance on reaction tests and 54% better physiological alertness than colleagues who stayed awake. The gains came in the final hours, near landing. A rest the length of a coffee break covered the hardest stretch.
move: Plan rest before the hard stretch, not after tiredness arrives.
ask: Where in my week could a short planned rest come just before my most demanding hour?
source: Rosekind et al., NASA Technical Memorandum, 1994
reference: Rosekind et al., Crew factors in flight operations IX: Effects of planned cockpit rest on crew performance and alertness in long-haul operations, NASA Technical Memorandum, 1994
